No task connects unrelated modules without a shared rationale.; Unambiguous Requirements — Requirements specify exact array contents, exact string replacements, exact return values (e.g. PASS_NEXT["task-impl"]=null), and cite grep commands as verifiable criteria. No vague adjectives found.; Complete Context — Each requirement provides sufficient specificity (exact function signatures, file paths, line approximations, expected values) that two independent reviewers could reach the same pass/fail judgment.; REQ Diff-Verifiability — All must requirements are decidable from diff (array literal order, value assignments) or test execution results. Requirements with testable:false rely only on grep-verifiable diff content, not future behavior guarantees.; No Hardcoded Secrets — The spec is a design document with no source code; no API keys, passwords, tokens, or secrets are present.; No Silent Error Swallowing — This is a spec/design document, not implementation code. No error handling patterns are prescribed or omitted.; Prioritize Requirements — All 16 requirements (R1–R16) each carry an explicit priority of 'must' or 'should'. No requirement is left unprioritized.; Impact on Existing Features — There is no explicit 'Impact on Existing Features' section or statement. The impact on existing active flow.json files (breaking change: old-order states silently become invalid) is only implied by the constraints section ('旧 state は再初期化を許容') rather than listed as a named impact. The guardrail requires an explicit listing or a statement that no existing features are affected.; Bounded Resource Usage — The change is a simple array-position swap with no recursive processing, retry loops, or bulk data loading introduced.; Spec Includes Test Strategy — Dedicated test tasks (T-2 exact-order unit test, T-3 state-based progression unit test, T-9 gate-phase-inference update, T-11 e2e integration test, T-12 stale-literal updates) and per-requirement acceptance criteria provide a comprehensive test strategy.; Synthesize Draft, Do Not Copy — The spec is structured with goal, background, scope, requirements, tasks, rationale, and alternatives—clearly synthesized rather than a raw draft copy. No invented content is apparent.; Record Unresolved Points as Open Questions — open_questions is explicitly empty; every design decision cites concrete evidence (grep hit counts, specific file lines, existing test references). No answers are fabricated.; Include 'Why This Approach' Rationale — The overview.decisions array provides rationale with evidence and consideredAlternatives for each design choice; the alternatives_considered section gives explicit rejection reasons for five alternatives.; Spec Test Coverage — The guardrail requires test code to be written under specs/<specid>/tests/. Most test tasks (T-3, T-9, T-11, T-12) direct tests exclusively to tests/unit/ or tests/e2e/; only T-2 mentions specs/251-fix-flow-impl-phase-order/tests/ as an option. The MUST placement requirement is not uniformly satisfied.; Backward-Compatible CLI Interface — The alpha-version policy (explicitly stated in constraints: '後方互換コードは書かない') serves as the stated migration plan—no migration is provided and this decision is explicitly justified. The alternatives_considered section also explicitly rejects a migration script and cites the alpha policy.; Exit Code Contract — No new CLI commands are introduced. Existing gate/review/next-action commands retain the same success/failure semantics; only internal next-hint values and phase-resolution mappings change.; Validate User Input at Entry Point — R11 references VALID_GATE_PHASES as the authoritative set and updates help text to match it, implying validation remains tied to that enumeration. No new user-facing arguments are introduced; the --phase argument's valid values are enumerated in the requirements.
